concepts.def: Liquid water becomes vapour at the surface of oceans, lakes and soils.
Loss of water vapour through plant stomata, drawing water from roots.
Water vapour cools and forms droplets, creating clouds.
Water returns to the surface as rain, snow, hail or sleet.
Surface water soaks into soil and rock, replenishing groundwater.
Surface flow of water across land into streams and rivers.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Water — a core area of GCSE Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Water brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Water.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
